paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is a LOT of names, and I want you to hear what all those names are saying. God gave Judah a real place, with borders on every side and cities and villages listed one by one. Joshua 15:20 sums it up: “This is the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Judah.” I think that tells us the gift was real, with a shape you could walk around.

Now look at Caleb. Joshua gave him Hebron “According to the LORD’s command to him” (Joshua 15:13), and Caleb still got up and drove out the three sons of Anak who were there (Joshua 15:14). Then Acsah says, “Give me a blessing,” and she gets both the upper and lower springs (Joshua 15:19). Friend, she asked and got springs on top of her land, so what's stopping you from asking?

The chapter ends on a hard note. Judah “could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem,” and the writer says “to this day the Jebusites live there among the descendants of Judah” (Joshua 15:63). I think that line stings a little, because the land was given and this one piece still wasn't cleared. The passage doesn't say why, so I won't guess, but I'm telling you, friend, the inheritance is still called Judah's inheritance (Joshua 15:20).
